context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Right now `security.isAuthorized()` only checks that the caller is logged in. Any authenticated user can call `GET /api/Complaints` and get every user's complaints, including their Personal Data. Add a middleware after `isAuthorized()` that reads the user ID from the verified JWT (for example `security.authenticatedUsers.from(req)?.data.id`) and adds `where: { UserId: <that id> }` to the query, so non-privileged users only get their own complaints. Only users with an authorised role, such as `security.isAccounting()` or an admin role check, should get the unfiltered list. Never take ownership from a `UserId` sent in the query, path or body. Apply the same check to every other method on the route (`GET /api/Complaints/:id`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`). For record-level routes, load the record and return 403 if its `UserId` doesn't match the token's user ID and the caller has no authorised role. For `POST`, set `UserId` from the token on the server and ignore any value the client sends. Then add tests confirming that user A gets only A's complaints, gets 403 on B's complaint by ID, and gets 401 without a token.
